title: Binding of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) to the PPARgamma/RXRalpha-DNA Complex.
authors: Almeida, Nuno M S; Bali, Semiha Kevser; James, Deepak; Wang, Cong; Wilson, Angela K
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文用MD和电子结构方法研究PFAS与PPARgamma/RXRalpha-DNA复合物（含DBD）的结合，属广义蛋白-DNA互作建模，方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系，但对象非典型TF-DNA特异性结合。
abstract: Nuclear receptors are the fundamental building blocks of gene expression regulation and the focus of many drug targets. While binding to DNA, nuclear receptors act as transcription factors, governing a multitude of functions in the human body. Peroxisome proliferator-activator receptor gamma (PPARgamma) and the retinoid X receptor alpha (RXRalpha) form heterodimers with unique properties and have a primordial role in insulin sensitization. This PPARgamma/RXRalpha heterodimer has been shown to be impacted by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and linked to a variety of significant health conditions in humans. Herein, a selection of the most common PFAS (legacy and emerging) was studied utilizing molecular dynamics simulations for PPARgamma/RXRalpha. The local and global structural effects of PFAS binding on the known ligand binding pockets of PPARgamma and RXRalpha as well as the DNA binding domain (DBD) of RXRalpha were inspected. The binding free energies were predicted computationally and were compared between the different binding pockets. In addition, two electronic structure approaches were utilized to model the interaction of PFAS within the DNA binding domain, density functional theory (DFT) and domain-based pair natural orbital coupled cluster with perturbative triples (DLPNO-CCSD(T)) approaches, with implicit solvation. Residue decomposition and hydrogen-bonding analysis were also performed, detailing the role of prominent residues in molecular recognition. The role of l-carnitine is explored as a potential in vivo remediation strategy for PFAS interaction with the PPARgamma/RXRalpha heterodimer. In this work, it was found that PFAS can bind and act as agonists for all of the investigated pockets. For the first time in the literature, PFAS are postulated to bind to the DNA binding domain in a nonspecific manner. In addition, for the PPARgamma ligand binding domain, l-carnitine shows promise in replacing smaller PFAS from the pocket.
abstract_zh: 核受体是基因表达调控的基本构建模块，也是众多药物靶点的焦点。在与DNA结合时，核受体作为转录因子发挥作用，调控人体内的多种功能。过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体γ（PPARgamma）和维甲酸X受体α（RXRalpha）形成具有独特性质的异二聚体，并在胰岛素增敏中发挥首要作用。该PPARgamma/RXRalpha异二聚体已被证明受到全氟和多氟烷基物质（PFAS）的影响，并与人类多种重大健康状况相关。在此，利用分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟研究了针对PPARgamma/RXRalpha的最常见PFAS（传统和新出现的）的选定集合。检查了PFAS结合对PPARgamma和RXRalpha已知配体结合口袋以及RXRalpha DNA结合域（DBD）的局部和全局结构效应。计算预测了结合自由能，并在不同结合口袋之间进行了比较。此外，采用两种电子结构方法模拟PFAS在DNA结合域内的相互作用，即密度泛函理论 (density functional theory, DFT) 和基于域的对自然轨道耦合簇微扰三激发 (DLPNO-CCSD(T)) 方法，并采用隐式溶剂化。还进行了残基分解和氢键分析，详细阐述了显著残基在分子识别中的作用。探讨了左卡尼汀作为PFAS与PPARgamma/RXRalpha异二聚体相互作用的潜在体内修复策略。在本工作中，发现PFAS能够结合并作为所有研究口袋的激动剂。文献中首次提出PFAS以非特异性方式结合到DNA结合域。此外，对于PPARgamma配体结合域，左卡尼汀在将较小PFAS从口袋中置换方面显示出潜力。
